questions.question: Name the four factors of production, give a South African example of each, and state the reward each earns.
questions.expected_answer: Natural resources (land), e.g. farmland, platinum, water, wind: rent. Labour, e.g. a nurse, teacher or mine worker: wages or salaries. Capital (man-made goods used in production), e.g. machines, a delivery van, an oven, roads: interest. Entrepreneurship, e.g. the founder of a car wash who organises the other factors and takes the risk: profit.

questions.question: A bakery has sales of R50 000. It pays rent R8 000, wages R22 000, interest R2 000 and ingredients R12 000. Calculate the profit and explain why profit is the reward for entrepreneurship.
questions.expected_answer: Profit = 50 000 - 8 000 - 22 000 - 2 000 - 12 000 = R6 000. Profit is the residual left after all contractual payments; the entrepreneur organises the factors and bears the risk of a loss, so profit rewards that risk.

questions.question: Distinguish between the goods and services market, the factor market and the financial market, stating who buys and who sells in each.
questions.expected_answer: Goods and services market: final goods and services are traded; businesses sell, households buy. Factor market: factors of production (mainly labour) are traded; households sell, businesses (and government) buy. Financial market: money is lent and borrowed and shares and bonds traded; savers (mainly households) supply funds through banks to borrowers (businesses and government); it includes the money market (short-term) and capital market (long-term, e.g. the JSE).
